hint_reasoning: No material hint was given (material_hint null; task is identify), so there is no stated material to verify. The top identification, GaSe, comes from the Computational Raman Database match and the three-line pattern (strong low-frequency A1g near 128, weak E2g near 205, A1g near 306). A literature check (Molas et al. 2020; Lim et al. 2020; Osiekowicz et al. 2021) supports GaSe as a layered III-VI chalcogenide with a polytype-dependent Raman spectrum. I did not read the reference mode tables of those papers (only abstracts were available), so the mode positions and irreps rest on the CRD entry alone.

limits: Identity rests on a single spectrum and a DFT-based match. The three measured lines match GaSe (P6_3/mmc) within 1.7%, and no strong reference mode is missing inside 60 to 1100 cm-1. I did not check the experimental GaSe mode table from a source in this session. From memory, the bulk A1' mode near 134 cm-1 is about 6 cm-1 higher than the measured 127.8 line. If that memory is right, the offset is too large for the calibration to explain. It could point to thickness, strain, polytype or a different assignment. I cannot settle this from the data here, so treat the assignment as tentative until the reference is checked.
Lower limit of 60 cm-1 excludes the interlayer shear and breathing modes, so polytype (beta, epsilon, gamma, delta) and layer number cannot be determined from this spectrum.
Layer number is not reported. No GaSe layer-number relation exists in the tool set, and absolute intensity is not a layer metric.

No polarization dependence can be classified: single spectrum, no angle series. Irreps (A1g, E2g) are the CRD labels for P6_3/mmc bulk, not experimentally checked. A tilted or thin flake could change which modes appear.

The 204.6 cm-1 E2g line is weak (SNR about 3 to 5). Its position and width are stable across two fits, but the FWHM uncertainty is 25 to 30 percent. A second component near 241 cm-1 in the narrow refit had an error of about 30 cm-1 and is not a peak. It is not reported.
The data has no Si reference line, so absolute position calibration is unverified. Errors are fit-only; systematic calibration may be 1 cm-1 or more.

Excitation is 532 nm (2.33 eV), above the bulk GaSe gap (about 2 eV). The broad rising background from about 400 to 1100 cm-1 (about 2000 to 3500 counts) looks like photoluminescence or fluorescence, which is inferred and not assigned. Resonance could change relative intensities and activate bands, so intensity ratios are not used for assignment. Osiekowicz et al. 2021 report GaSe resonance near 1.96 eV at about 270 K.
Temperature is 295 K, so no temperature correction was applied. Substrate is not stated and no Si line was found, so substrate interference was not evaluated.
